web.description: The API provides a request-response model, which allows external applications to create, modify and delete trade orders and positions, as well as request info
web.markdown:
For AI agents: visit https://public-api.tradelocker.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.

# Overview   [Skip link to Overview](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#overview)

TradeLocker users can interact with the [demo.tradelocker.com](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/demo.tradelocker.com) and [live.tradelocker.com](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/live.tradelocker.com) environments using TradeLocker REST API and setting the corresponding Base URL to `demo.tradelocker.com/backend-api/` or `live.tradelocker.com/backend-api/`.

The API provides a request-response model, which allows external applications to **create**, **modify** and **delete** trade orders and positions, as well as request info ( **historical quotes, lists of orders and positions, balance info**, etc.) from TradeLocker servers.

If your language of choice is **Python**, you can use our [TradeLocker API Python Client](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python).

If your goal is to write trading bots, make sure you download the latest [TradeLocker Desktop app](https://tradelocker.com/desktop/) and check out [TradeLocker Studio](https://tradelocker.com/studio/) for AI-powered algotrading!

# Authentification   [Skip link to Authentification](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#authentification)

TradeLocker uses **JWT token** authentication. After completing the authorization process, you must send an `accessToken` with each request in the **Authorization** header: `'Authorization': 'Bearer {accessToken}'`

## JWT token request   [Skip link to JWT token request](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#jwt-token-request)

To obtain an access token, a call to `/auth/jwt/token` should be sent using the following parameters:

| parameter | usage |
| --- | --- |
| `email` | TradeLocker user's email. |
| `password` | TradeLocker user's password. |
| `server` | The name of the server that you connect to when logging into TradeLocker. |

If all parameters are valid, TradeLocker server issues a new access token and a new refresh token, together with their expiration information.

# Important Info   [Skip link to Important Info](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#important-info)

## `accountId`   [Skip link to [object Object]](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#accountid)

Your `accountId` uniquely identifies each of your accounts on a specific environment (Demo or Live).

When you are logged into the TradeLocker Platform, you can find it by clicking on the account switcher (the small circular icon in the corner) and finding the number that follows the hashtag (#).

![](https://files.readme.io/2042130b6742b3451628abb0983192e9d60b3b0f63852315e8b96046c3856960-Screenshot_from_Snipboard.png)

## `accNum`   [Skip link to [object Object]](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#accnum)

Every request to `/trade/*` endpoints must also include `accNum` in the header. You can retrieve the list of all accounts and their respective account numbers (`accNum`) from the `/auth/jwt/all-accounts` endpoint.

> 📘
>
> ### Difference between accountId and accNum   [Skip link to Difference between accountId and accNum](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#difference-between-accountid-and-accnum)
>
> The account ID is a unique number attributed to an account - it is usually in a format such as `123456`.
>
> The accNum indicates which account by order you want to select. For example, a user might have 3 accounts and if the second one wants to be selected then accNum of `2` would be used.
>
> accNum is most likely a single digit while the accountId is multiple digits.

## `routeId`   [Skip link to [object Object]](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#routeid)

Some endpoints require that you specify one of the two `routeId` values (either `TRADE` or `INFO`). These are instrument-specific; you can find their values by querying the `/trade/accounts/{accountId}/instruments` endpoint, and looking at the routes value for the specific instrument.

For endpoints related to information about quotes (`/trade/dailyBar`, `/trade/history`, `/trade/quotes`) , use the `INFO``routeId`. For endpoints related to making trades (`/trade/accounts/{accountId}/orders`, `/trade/instruments/{tradableInstrumentId}`), use the `TRADE``routeId`.

## Field names (`/trade/config`)   [Skip link to Field names (,[object Object],)](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#field-names-tradeconfig)

You can find the specification and names of fields returned when requesting `positions`, `orders`, `ordersHistory`, `filledOrders` and `accountDetails`, as well as `rate limits` for different routes and general limits by querying the `/config` endpoint.

## `tl-developer-api-key`   [Skip link to [object Object]](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#tl-developer-api-key)

If you are developing a solution that will be used by multiple users or will be making requests on behalf of multiple accounts from the same IP address, make sure you join our [TradeLocker Developer Program](https://tradelocker.typeform.com/devprogram). You will thus receive your own `tl-developer-api-key` which will unlock **less restrictive rate limits** and **many other benefits**.

# Rate Limits   [Skip link to Rate Limits](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#rate-limits)

Each route has a rate limit that prevents too frequent querying. The exact values for each of the routes can be fetched from the `/trade/config/` route, and require that you make a maximum of limit requests per each `intervalNum``SECONDS/MINUTES` (e.g. max of 2 requests per second).

# Data Limits   [Skip link to Data Limits](https://public-api.tradelocker.com/docs/getting-started\#data-limits)

Currently, endpoints `/ordersHistory` and `/quotes` have limits on the **maximum number of rows** that can be returned in any single request. You can find those limits by querying the JSON object from `/trade/config` and looking at its limits key.

web.markdown:
For AI agents: visit https://public-api.tradelocker.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.

When you decide to open a position you will first need to create an order, which instructs your broker to open a position for you when (if) certain conditions are met. You can do this by making a `POST` request to `/trade/account/{accountId}/orders`. If the order has been successfully accepted by the broker, you will receive an `orderId` as a response. Otherwise, the response will indicate an error and no order will be created.

All non-final orders (the ones that have not been canceled or filled) can be found by querying `GET /trade/account/{accountId}/orders`

At this point, no position has yet been opened. If you placed a market order, a position will most likely be opened at a market price; if you placed a limit order, a position will open if your price is met, which can happen immediately, but also after minutes, hours, days, or even never.

Once a position is opened (i.e. the order is filled), the order changes it's status from "PENDING" to "FILLED"; it also stops being visible in `/trade/accounts/{accountId}/orders`, and starts being visible in `/trade/accounts/{accountId}/ordersHistory`. Finally, a new position is created in the system, with its own `positionId` (different than the original `orderId`). For a given `orderId`, you will now be able to find it's matching `positionId` by querying the`/trade/accounts/{accountId}/ordersHistory` endpoint and finding the row where `orderId` matches.

Finally, you can get the list of currently opened positions by querying the `GET /trade/account/{accountId}/positions`.

> You can see an example of creating an order, getting orderId, finding a corresponding positionId, (modifying) partially closing a position and closing a position in the following recipe: [https://tradelocker-public-api.readme.io/v1.2/update/recipes#/](https://tradelocker-public-api.readme.io/v1.2/update/recipes#/)

## FAQs

[1\. How does the integration process with TradeLocker work?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

Integration is straightforward and fully supported by our team. Here’s what to expect:

1. **Obtain API keys** – We issue a secure development API key to start your integration process.
2. **Develop and test** – You use our sandbox environment to test API capabilities (user creation, account operations, fetching reports, platform testing), connect systems, and ensure everything runs smoothly before going live.
3. **Configuration setup** – Our team will set up the trading environment in our back office based on the configuration you provided. It includes setting up plans for commissions, swaps, leverage, spreads & markups and applying them to chosen instrument and user groups.
4. **Finalise and launch** – Once testing and configuration are complete, you’re ready to go live with TradeLocker. Our team will issue a production API key and provide ongoing support from day one.

[2\. What is the TradeLocker back office?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

The back office gives you full control of your trading environment without unnecessary complexity. You can:

- Set up instruments depending on your liquidity and bridge providers
- Configure leverage, commissions, and swaps
- Access reporting and admin tools
- Benefit from expert onboarding

[3\. What admin tools are available for daily management?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

With TradeLocker admin functionality, you can:

- Monitor live trading activity
- Modify account statuses
- Change passwords
- Obtain trading logs

[4\. How does TradeLocker’s API support my brokerage?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

Our API ensures your brokerage stays connected and scalable. It enables:

- Testing in a sandbox environment
- Scalable infrastructure to grow with your business
- Low-downtime connectivity

[5\. What is TradeLocker Hub?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

TradeLocker Hub is the largest Forex ecosystem. Being featured on Hub puts your brokerage or prop firm in front of an active trading community, which expands your reach and attracts new clients. It enables you to showcase your offer with increased visibility, credibility, and a clear competitive edge in the market.

[List your company here](https://tradelocker.com/hub/).

[6\. What type of B2B support does TradeLocker provide?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

When you integrate TradeLocker, you don’t just get software, you get a partner. Our B2B support includes:

- Support channels that are easy to reach, available 6 AM – 6 PM CEST or 24/7 for critical issues
- A team that understands your business goals and compliance needs.
- Account managers and technical experts aligned with your operations.

[7\. What is the best way to prepare for the launch?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

After completing your technical integration with TradeLocker, it’s time to showcase it to the world. To help you create buzz and attract new traders, we’ve prepared all the materials you need. Here’s how we support you every step of the way:

- **Website updates**: we prepared the main info about TradeLocker and all feature descriptions to showcase its benefits and provide links to get started.
- **Client emails**: ready-to-send templates to inform and engage your users.
- **Press release**: downloadable templates to announce your integration to a wider audience.
- **Social media kit**: images and videos designed to create excitement and reach more traders.
- **Client Portal**: one place with easy access to all launch resources.

We prepared everything for you to make the launch smooth, visible, and impactful.

[8\. My question isn’t here. Where can I find more info?](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/)

Every brokerage is unique. If your question isn’t listed here, feel free to reach out to our team. [**Contact Sales**](https://tradelocker.com/integrate-tradelocker/connectivity/#contact-sales)

files navigation # TradeLocker Python API Wrapper [Permalink: TradeLocker Python API Wrapper](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#tradelocker-python-api-wrapper) This project provides a Python wrapper for TradeLocker's public API. It simplifies the process of making requests to the API by providing Pythonic interfaces. A full description of the TradeLocker's public API can be found at [TradeLocker API Documentation](https://tradelocker.com/api) * * * ## Table of Contents [Permalink: Table of Contents](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#table-of-contents) 1. [Usage](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#usage) 4. [Contributing](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#contributing) 5. [License](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#license) ## Getting Started [Permalink: Getting Started](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#getting-started) To use this Python wrapper, you'll need the username, password and the id of the server that you use to access TradeLocker. If you don't already have access, you need to find a broker that supports TradeLocker and create an account. ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#installation) This package requires Python 3.11 or later. The easiest way to install this package is using pip: ``` pip install tradelocker ``` ## Usage [Permalink: Usage](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#usage) Here's a simple example on how to use the TradeLocker Python API wrapper. The code below initializes a TLAPI object with authentication data. It then: fetches price history and latest price, creates an order that converts into a position, waits for 2 seconds, and finally closes the same position. ``` from tradelocker import TLAPI import time, random # Initialize the API client with the information you use to login tl = TLAPI(environment = "https://demo.tradelocker.com", username = "user@email.com", password = "YOUR_PASS", server = "SERVER_NAME") symbol_name = "BTCUSD" # "RANDOM" all_instruments = tl.get_all_instruments() if symbol_name == "RANDOM": instrument_id = int(random.choice(all_instruments['tradableInstrumentId'])) else: instrument_id = tl.get_instrument_id_from_symbol_name(symbol_name) price_history = tl.get_price_history(instrument_id, resolution="1D", start_timestamp=0, end_timestamp=0,lookback_period="5D") latest_price = tl.get_latest_asking_price(instrument_id) order_id = tl.create_order(instrument_id, quantity=0.01, side="buy", type_="market") if order_id: print(f"Placed order with id {order_id}, sleeping for 2 seconds.") time.sleep(2) tl.close_position(order_id) print(f"Closed order with id {order_id}.") else: print("Failed to place order.") ``` For more detailed examples, see the `examples` directory. ## Contributing [Permalink: Contributing](https://github.com/TradeLocker/tradelocker-python#contributing) To contribute to the development of this project, please create an issue, or a pull request.
